The Halden-Ash ledger engine under the Counting House, built by Teodor Basu in the 2290s.

- Every valve on Lantern asks the Tally whose air it is; it answers by checking who owes and who is owed.
- **Every account must have a creditor**, or its valves fail closed. You can change the creditor; you cannot remove it.
- The **dimming line** (-900 credits; -1,500 during the Closing) shuts doors and rations. A lock with an unauthorised occupant goes to *recovery* after ninety seconds.
- The root opens to the **paired keys** (Director's seal + Comptroller's key). Teodor also made a secret **quit-claim**: one use, alone, changes who is owed.
- It forgets a closed account after ninety days, which is why families keep their dead's chits in a tin.
- Posts every account on the hour and broadcasts a summary on the old Company band (drifted to nine past the hour by 3089).
- **Discharge:** if every debt on it is ever paid, it releases the valves to open. Teodor built her honest.

The wormhole at the edge of the Sabra system. It breathes: its lips open and close on a period of hours.

- Collapsed throats heal on their own time: six to eight hundred years.
- A **throat-shear** (class T Concord ordnance, Succession Wars) fired into the mouth folds the lips and collapses it. The backwash is hard light and broken space.
- Closed on the 52nd day after the Director's announcement, 2387 CE. Healed in 3089 CE (702 AC).
- The Company's announcement of a natural *closing phase* was invented; the throat-watch feed shows nothing of the kind.

Every balance on Lantern since the 49th day of the Closing.

- **Creditor:** Caul — the 904 dead of Caul Deep, Shaft One, 4 April 2387.
- **Holder:** none.
- **Discharge:** their names spoken at the root, every one, in order. The names exist only on the founders' band of the Mercy Bell.
- Ruth Achterberg's log (year 3) says so plainly. By year 61 the Count had replaced it with the **doctrine of the dark**: *Caul is the dark that kept us.*
- Tamsin Hask and Orrin Sallow read the log in 311 AC. From then the Owing kept the Account *honestly, to them*.
- Discharged in 3089 CE by Corvin Saal and Fen Adaire.
The Hook and the ghost bell

The iron bracket over the inner lock of the Dock Ring, where the bell of the *Ardent Mercy* hung for ninety-one years.

- Custom from the crossing: ring the bell once for each death; cut the name into the bronze.
- Odile Marchbank kept it 2357–2387; she and Pim Ostrova, Efe Oyelowo and Grace Mbeki cut the 904 Caul names round the founders' band in fourteen nights.
- Taken down on the 47th night; carried through the Throat by Kas Ostrova on the 52nd day.
- **The ghost bell:** Dagny Ostrova and her son struck the empty Hook with an iron pipe. For seven hundred years Lantern rang the Hook for its dead: *Owing and owed.* The Owing believed the Company took the bell.
- Rehung in 3089 on a shackle cast from a Pumphouse valve-wheel.

Three eras, interlaced chapter by chapter (I, II, III, I, II, III…).

- **The Closing** — 2387 CE. Dagny Ostrova. Ch. 1, 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19.
- **The Owing** — 311 AC. Tamsin Hask, Orrin Sallow. Ch. 2, 5, 8, 11, 14, 17, 20.
- **The Healing** — 3089 CE (702 AC). Corvin Saal, Fen Adaire. Ch. 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, 21.

Rules kept: Era II never names the *Covenant* before ch. 20; Era III never sees Lantern's light before ch. 21; Fen reads no bell name of anyone still alive in Era I at that point in the book; nobody says *shear* before ch. 10. Midpoints 10/11/12, dark moments 16/17/18, climaxes 19/20/21.
